# Iterator Module Skeleton Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Create the `src/iter/` module skeleton and the internal `StrideState` helper used for F-order traversal of non-contiguous layouts.

**Architecture:** `mod.rs` declares `elements`, `axis`, and `indexed`. `StrideState` stays private and implements the documented F-order carry algorithm: increment the lowest axis first and carry upward on overflow.

**Tech Stack:** Rust, crate-internal helper state, no new dependencies

**Design Docs:** `design/10-iterator.md` §3, §5.1, §6.1, §6.2, §7 T1, §7 T2; `design/00-coding.md` §2, §3, §6

**Prerequisites:** W8T1 (`src/tensor/mod.rs`) must be complete.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the private `StrideState` helper in `src/iter/elements.rs`**

```rust
use crate::dimension::Dimension;

pub(crate) struct StrideState<D: Dimension> {
    shape: D,
    index: D,
    finished: bool,
}

impl<D: Dimension> StrideState<D> {
    pub(crate) fn new(shape: D, index: D) -> Self {
        let finished = shape.slice().iter().any(|&dim| dim == 0);
        Self { shape, index, finished }
    }

    pub(crate) fn index(&self) -> &D {
        &self.index
    }

    pub(crate) fn is_finished(&self) -> bool {
        self.finished
    }

    pub(crate) fn advance(&mut self) {
        if self.finished {
            return;
        }

        for i in 0..self.shape.ndim() {
            self.index[i] += 1;
            if self.index[i] < self.shape[i] {
                return;
            }
            self.index[i] = 0;
        }

        self.finished = true;
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::StrideState;
    use crate::dimension::IxDyn;

    #[test]
    fn test_stride_state_increment() {
        let mut state = StrideState::new(IxDyn::from(vec![2, 3]), IxDyn::from(vec![0, 0]));
        assert_eq!(state.index().slice(), &[0, 0]);
        state.advance();
        assert_eq!(state.index().slice(), &[1, 0]);
        state.advance();
        assert_eq!(state.index().slice(), &[0, 1]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_stride_state_empty_shape() {
        let state = StrideState::new(IxDyn::from(vec![0, 3]), IxDyn::from(vec![0, 0]));
        assert!(state.is_finished());
    }
}
```
